app_tagline: Open-source incident management that deploys to your Cloudflare account.

match.env=local, part=overview: The dashboard, its Worker, the API Worker and a Durable Object, all running on your machine.
match.env=dev, part=overview: A development deployment on Cloudflare, for trying changes: the dashboard, its Worker, the API Worker and a Durable Object.
match.env=dev, part=hint: Look for the error in this deployment's Worker logs, then check again.
match.env=staging, part=overview: A staging deployment on Cloudflare, for trying a release before production: the dashboard, its Worker, the API Worker and a Durable Object.
match.env=staging, part=hint: Look for the error in this deployment's Worker logs, then check again.
match.env=*, part=overview: Your workspace's incidents, who is on call, and who gets paged.

stack_api_down: The API Worker is not responding
stack_do_down: The Durable Object did not answer
stack_error_timeout: The request took longer than {seconds} seconds and was cancelled.
stack_error_invalid: The API answered, but not with the data the dashboard expects.
stack_hint_start: Start everything from the repository root, then check again:
stack_hint_do: The API is up. Look for the error in the terminal running:
legend_description: How incidents are marked across Brigade. The code or the name always travels with the colour.
stack_error_unreachable: The web Worker couldn't reach the API Worker.
stack_hint_api_error: The API answered with an error. Look for it in the terminal running:
stack_api_error: The API Worker is answering with errors
stack_api_stuck: The API Worker is not answering in time
stack_hint_api_stuck: The API looks like it is running but stuck. Look in the terminal running:
paging_unreachable: Couldn't check whether pages get through
paging_unknown: The paging self-check hasn't run yet. Once it runs, a heartbeat goes through Brigade's event queue every minute and checks that the push relay accepts Brigade's token. It doesn't send anything to phones.
paging_reason_pipeline_stalled: The self-check's heartbeat stopped getting through the event queue, or gets through minutes late.
paging_reason_pipeline_slow: The self-check's heartbeat takes more than two minutes to get through the event queue.
paging_reason_relay_unauthorized: The push relay refused Brigade's send token, so no page can go out.
paging_reason_relay_not_configured: No push relay is set up, so every page is recorded as failed.
mobile_overview_description: The severity and status legend, drawn from the shared tokens and catalog.
intl_description: What this JavaScript engine provides on its own, and what the shared helpers render with it.
sync_reconnecting_hint: Showing the last list received. Changes you make are sent once the connection is back.
sync_unavailable_hint: Couldn't connect to Brigade Sync. For now it only runs in the local stack, started from the repository root:
sync_retrying: This page keeps trying on its own.
sync_error_forbidden: You don't have permission to do that.
sync_error_invalid_transition: Its status changed in the meantime, so that move is no longer allowed.
sync_error_invalid_args: Check what you typed and try again.
sync_error_expired: It waited too long to be sent and was dropped.
sync_error_too_many_pending: Wait for the pending changes to be sent, then try again.
sync_error_closed: This page stopped syncing. Reload it to try again.
sync_error_internal: Something went wrong on the server. Try again.
sync_error_limit_reached: You've reached the limit for this.
declare_title_invalid: A title needs visible text: invisible characters alone don't count.
sync_error_read_forbidden: You don't have access to these incidents.
sync_offline_hint: Can't reach Brigade right now. Changes you make are sent when the connection is back, as long as this page stays open.
sync_error_clock_skew: Your device clock is ahead of the server. Fix the date and time and try again.
declare_sent: Sent “{title}”. It shows here once the list loads.
mobile_sync_retrying: The app keeps trying on its own.
mobile_sync_offline_hint: Can't reach Brigade right now. Changes you make are kept if you close Brigade, and sent once it's open and can reach the server.

match.part=sign_in_hint: New to Brigade? Create an account on the dashboard, then sign in here.

auth_error_network: Could not reach Brigade. Check your connection and try again.
workspace_error_limit: You belong to as many workspaces as Brigade allows. Ask an owner to add you instead.
workspace_name_invalid: A name needs visible text: invisible characters alone don't count.

match.action=prompt: Pause this monitor? Its checks stop until you resume it.
match.action=prompt_alert: Pause this monitor? Its checks stop until you resume it, and its firing alert resolves.

match.field=url: Use a public http or https address, on a web port such as 80, 443, 8080 or 8443.
match.field=host: Use a public host name or IP address, without http:// or a port.
match.field=host_cloudflare: Cloudflare doesn't allow TCP checks of its own addresses. Use your server's address.
match.field=host_underscore: Host names can't contain underscores (_). Use a public host name or IP address.
match.field=port_blocked: Cloudflare blocks port 25. Use another port.
match.field=expected_status: Use a status from 100 to 599, or leave it empty.
match.field=interval: Use whole seconds, from 30 to 86,400 (24 hours).
match.field=timeout: Use 1 to 30 seconds, and no more than the interval.
match.field=grace: Use whole seconds, from 0 to 86,400 (24 hours).
match.field=policy: That policy no longer exists. Pick another.

match.field=url: Everyone in the workspace, viewers too, can see this URL: keep tokens and passwords out of it.
match.field=expected_status: Empty: any 2xx or 3xx. Redirects are not followed.
match.field=host: Passes when a connection to this host and port opens; nothing is sent. Hosts proxied by Cloudflare can't be checked over TCP.
match.field=timeout: How long one check may take.
match.field=timeout_tcp: How long the connection may take to open.
match.field=policy: An incident this monitor opens pages through this policy.
match.field=*: How late a ping may be before it counts as missed.

match.part=send: Send a POST to this URL at least every {interval}. Brigade keeps only a hash of it, so it can't be shown again.
match.part=close_prompt: Close without copying? The URL can't be shown again.

match.part=restart: Saving starts its checks over: the last results are dropped and it shows Waiting until its regions report again.
match.part=restart_alert: Its firing alert stays until its checks pass again.

match.part=prompt: Delete {name}? Its checks stop and its results are gone for good.
match.part=alert: Its firing alert resolves. The incident it opened is left for people to close.
match.part=incidents: Incidents it opened before stay as they are.

match.part=hint: Brigade keeps only a hash of it, so the current URL can't be shown again. A new one replaces it.
match.part=stops: The current URL stops working at once; update whatever pings it.
match.part=restart: The monitor starts over from Waiting, with a full interval and grace before a missed ping counts.
match.part=restart_alert: Its firing alert stays until the new URL is pinged.
match.part=unsaved: Your other changes in this form won't be saved.
match.part=shown: New URL for {name}, shown only once

match.part=not_found: There is no incident with this number in this workspace.
match.part=update_placeholder: What do you know now? What happens next?
match.part=update_hint: Everyone in the workspace sees it on the timeline.
match.part=update_invalid: Remove invisible, control or bidi characters and try again.
match.part=no_members: Teammates show up here once they have opened Brigade.
match.part=read_only: Viewers follow the incident; responders and admins change it.

match.part=placeholder: Search a city or UTC offset

match.part=declined_body: You won't join {workspace}. Whoever invited you can send a new invitation.
match.part=sign_in_title: Sign in to see this invitation
match.part=sign_in_body: Sign in, or create an account, with the email address the invitation was sent to.
match.part=wrong_email_title: This invitation is for another email address
match.part=wrong_email_body: You're signed in as {email}. Sign out, then sign in with the address the invitation was sent to.
match.part=unverified_body: We sent a link to {email}. Open it, and you'll come back here.
match.part=expired_body: Ask whoever invited you to send it again.
match.part=gone_title: This invitation is no longer available
match.part=gone_body: It was already accepted, declined or revoked.
match.part=not_found_body: Check that you opened the whole link from the email.
match.part=decline_prompt: Decline the invitation to {workspace}? To join later, you'd need a new invitation.

match.reason=workspace_full: {workspace} has reached its member limit. Ask an owner to make room.
match.reason=workspace_limit: You already belong to as many workspaces as Brigade allows. Leave one first.
match.reason=conflict: The invitation changed meanwhile. Reload the page.
match.reason=not_applied: You joined. Paging catches up on its own within a minute.
match.reason=unavailable: Brigade couldn't reach its database. Nothing changed; try again.
match.reason=network: Couldn't reach Brigade. Check your connection and try again.

auth_error_email_not_verified: Confirm your email first: open the link Brigade sent you, then sign in.
auth_sign_up_invited_description: Use the address the invitation was sent to. After you confirm it, you can accept the invitation.

match.part=intro: Someone asked to reset the password of the Brigade account for {email}. If it was you, choose a new password with this link.
match.part=expires: The link works once, for 1 hour. Setting a new password signs the account out everywhere, including phones, and confirms this email address.
match.part=footer: If you didn't ask for this, ignore this email: your password stays as it is.

match.part=forgot_description: Enter the email you signed up with. We'll send you a link to choose a new password.
match.part=sent_body: If {email} has a Brigade account, a link to choose a new password is on its way. It works for 1 hour. Check spam too.
match.part=rate_limited: Too many links asked for this address. Try again in an hour.
match.part=not_configured: This Brigade server can't send email yet. Ask whoever runs it.
match.part=failed: Couldn't send the link. Try again.
match.part=reset_description: Saving it signs your account out everywhere, including the app on your phone.
match.part=done_body: Sign in with your new password. Every session was signed out, and your email address is confirmed. Your phones get no pages until you sign in to the app again.
match.part=invalid_body: It may have expired (links work for 1 hour), been used already, or been cut off. Ask for a new one.
match.part=uncertain: Brigade hit an error after receiving your new password, so it may already be saved. Try signing in with it; if that doesn't work, ask for a new link.

match.part=body: Someone signed up with your email address before you confirmed it, and created the workspaces below. They're yours now. So nobody else can page you through what they set up, Brigade paused every monitor there and turned off their heartbeat URLs.
match.part=after: Resume the monitors you want to keep. Give each heartbeat you keep a new URL (New URL in its Edit form) before you resume it. Check each workspace's on-call schedules and escalation policies too.
match.part=failed: Brigade couldn't reach this workspace, so nothing in it was paused. Check its monitors now.
match.part=dismiss_failed: Couldn't hide this notice. Try again.

match.part=reply_ambiguous: More than one incident is waiting to be acknowledged: {list}. Say which one, for example /inc ack {incident}.
match.part=reply_none: No active incident is waiting to be acknowledged.
match.part=reply_forbidden: Your role in {workspace} can't do that. Ask an owner or admin.
match.part=reply_unmapped: Your Slack email isn't the confirmed email of a member of {workspace} in Brigade, so Brigade can't act for you. Use the same email in both and confirm it in Brigade, or ask an owner to add you.
match.part=reply_unconfirmed: Brigade can't tell who you are: Slack hasn't confirmed your email, or you're a guest from another Slack workspace.
match.part=reply_not_connected: This Slack workspace isn't connected to Brigade. An owner or admin can connect it from the Brigade dashboard.
match.part=reply_reconnect: Brigade can't use this Slack workspace's connection any more. An owner or admin needs to connect Slack again from the Brigade dashboard.
match.part=reply_invalid_title: An incident needs a title of 1 to 200 characters, with no invisible characters.
match.part=reply_failed: Brigade couldn't do that right now. Try again in a moment.
match.part=usage: Declare an incident: /inc declare <title> [sev1, sev2, sev3 or sev4]. Acknowledge one: /inc ack [INC-12].

match.part=description: Declare and acknowledge incidents from Slack with /inc, and keep one message per incident in a channel.
match.part=load_failed: Couldn't load the Slack connection, so Brigade can't tell whether it's connected.
match.part=not_connected: Not connected to a Slack workspace.
match.part=channel_hint: In Slack, open the channel's details and copy the ID at the bottom. It starts with C, or G for a private channel, where Brigade must be invited.
match.part=channel_invalid: A channel ID starts with C or G, followed by capital letters and numbers.
match.part=channel_none: No channel yet, so incidents aren't posted to Slack.
match.part=disconnect_confirm: Disconnect {team}? /inc stops working there and incidents are no longer posted. To revoke Brigade's access, also remove the app in Slack's settings.
match.part=manage_only: Only owners and admins can connect Slack or change where incidents are posted.
match.part=result_connected: Slack is connected. Pick a channel for incidents.
match.part=result_team_taken: That Slack workspace is already connected to another Brigade workspace.
match.part=result_not_configured: Slack isn't set up on this Brigade server.

match.part=overall_degraded: Some systems are slower than usual
match.part=history_empty: No incidents in the last 90 days.
match.part=not_found_body: This address has no status page, or it isn't public right now.
match.part=unavailable_body: The status page can't be shown right now. Try again in a minute.

match.part=description: A public page where customers see which parts of your service work and what you tell them about incidents. Nothing from the internal timeline appears there unless someone publishes it.
match.part=load_failed: Couldn't load the status page settings.
match.part=manage_only: Only owners and admins can set up the status page or change its components.
match.part=title_hint: Usually your company's or product's name.
match.part=title_required: The page needs a name of up to 80 characters, without invisible characters.
match.part=slug_hint: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.
match.part=slug_invalid: Use 3 to 40 lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or number.
match.part=enabled_hint: Anyone with the address can read it. Off, it's a draft only members see here.
match.part=slug_taken: Another workspace already uses that address. Pick another one.
match.part=not_applied: Saved, but the page may take a minute to show it.
match.part=components_hint: What the page lists, for example API or Website. A group puts components together under one heading.
match.part=component_status_hint: The page shows the worse of this and the impact of any open incident published on it.
match.part=add_failed: Couldn't add the component. Try again.
match.part=limit: A status page can list at most 50 components.
match.part=delete_confirm: Delete {name}? It's taken off the page and out of every incident published on it.
match.part=publish_none: Nothing about this incident is on the status page.
match.part=publish_not_set_up: Set up a status page in the dashboard to tell customers about incidents.
match.part=publish_viewer: Owners, admins and responders can publish to the status page.
match.part=publish_hint: Written for the public: it appears on the status page as you write it. The internal timeline stays private.
match.part=public_title_required: The public needs a title, without invisible characters.
match.part=public_body_required: Write what the public should know.
match.part=cache_window: Changes reach visitors within about 2 minutes: until then, caches may still show the page as it was.
match.part=update_remove_confirm: Remove this update from the status page? Visitors may still see it for about 2 minutes, until caches catch up. The timeline keeps a record.
match.part=withdraw_confirm: Take this incident and all its updates off the status page? Visitors may still see it for about 2 minutes, until caches catch up. The timeline keeps a record.
match.part=withdrawn: Taken off the page. Visitors may still see it for about 2 minutes.
match.part=corrected: Corrected. Visitors may still see the old version for about 2 minutes.
match.part=correct_failed: Couldn't change the status page. Try again.

match.text=services_empty: No services yet. List what you run, who owns it and how critical it is, so incidents can say what they affect.
match.text=policy_note: Kept for alert routes: pages still go through the incident type's policy, the monitor's, or the default one.
match.text=not_found: There is no such service in this workspace. It may have been deleted.
match.text=active_none: No active incident names this service.
match.text=delete_service: Delete {name}? Incidents that name it stop showing it.
match.text=delete_type: Delete {name}? Its incidents keep their fields and show the type as deleted.
match.text=delete_field: Delete {name}? Its values stop showing on every incident, and types stop requiring it.
match.text=types_empty: No incident types yet. A type sets the severity a declare starts with, the escalation policy its pages use and the fields it needs.
match.text=fields_empty: No custom fields yet. A field adds a typed detail to every incident: text, one choice, several choices, a number or a link.
match.text=pages_default: No policy of its own: the monitor's or the default one pages
match.text=kind_fixed: A field's kind can't change once it exists.
match.text=required_note: Required fields never hold up declaring, paging or resolving; once filled they can change but not be cleared.
match.text=catalog_link: Edit types and fields on the overview.
match.text=dropped: People or schedules that are gone were taken out of the owners.

match.field=add_owner, form=label: Add a schedule or a person
match.field=description, form=invalid: Use at most 500 characters, without hidden characters.
match.field=options, form=invalid: Give every option a name, each one different.
match.field=text, form=invalid: Use 1 to 500 characters, without hidden characters.
match.field=link, form=invalid: Enter a link that starts with https:// or http://.

match.part=description: Send signed JSON to your own services when incidents, alerts and monitors change.
match.part=manage_only: Only owners and admins can see and manage webhooks.
match.part=empty: No endpoints yet. Add one to get incidents, alerts and monitor changes as signed JSON.
match.part=not_configured: Webhooks aren't set up on this Brigade server.
match.part=limit: A workspace can have at most 20 endpoints. Delete one to add another.
match.part=url_hint: HTTPS only, on a public host. Brigade doesn't follow redirects.
match.part=url_invalid: Enter an https:// URL on a public host, without a user name or password.
match.part=description_hint: Optional. Shown here instead of the host.
match.part=exists: This endpoint already exists. Give it a new secret if you missed the first one.
match.part=disabled_failing: Brigade turned this endpoint off {when}, after its deliveries kept failing for a day. Fix the endpoint, then turn it back on.
match.part=test_sent: Test event on its way. It shows under Recent deliveries.
match.part=test_too_soon: A test event went out moments ago. Wait a few seconds.
match.part=test_failed: Couldn't send a test event. Try again.
match.part=rotate_confirm: Give {host} a new signing secret? Deliveries are signed with both for 24 hours, so the receiver can switch over.
match.part=rotate_failed: Couldn't make a new secret. Try again.
match.part=delete_confirm: Delete {host}? Deliveries stop at once and its log is gone.
match.part=secret_created: Copy the signing secret for {host} now: Brigade won't show it again.
match.part=secret_rotated: New signing secret for {host}. Copy it now: Brigade won't show it again.
match.part=secret_verify: Check the webhook-signature header with any Standard Webhooks library, using this secret.
match.part=close_prompt: Close without copying? You'd have to make a new secret.
match.part=recent_empty: Nothing delivered yet. Send a test event to try the endpoint.

match.error=blocked: Blocked: not a public https URL

match.part=subject: A webhook in {workspace} was turned off
match.part=intro: Brigade turned off the webhook {webhook} in {workspace}: its last {failures} deliveries failed, over more than a day.
match.part=how: Fix the endpoint, then turn it back on from the Webhooks card on the dashboard. Events from while it was off aren't sent.
match.part=footer: You get this email because you're an owner of {workspace} on Brigade.
match.part=*: A webhook in {workspace} was turned off

match.text=description: What this incident leaves to do, with an owner and a due date.
match.text=title_placeholder: Add a retry budget to the payment client
match.text=link_invalid: Enter a link that starts with http:// or https://.
match.text=delete_confirm: Remove {name}? It stays on the timeline.
match.text=limit: This incident has as many follow-ups as it can hold. Remove a done one first.
match.text=read_only: Only responders, admins and owners change follow-ups.
match.text=open_description: Every open follow-up in the workspace, soonest due first.
match.text=open_empty: Nothing open. Follow-ups added to incidents show up here until they're done.

match.part=description: What happened and what the team learned, section by section. Plain text.
match.part=conflict: Someone saved the postmortem while you were editing. Your text is still here: copy what you need, then reload their version.
match.part=ai_hint: Workers AI writes a first draft from the timeline, updates and follow-ups. Nobody's email or devices are sent.
match.part=ai_marker_hint: Written by Workers AI from the timeline. Check every section; saving marks it as reviewed.
match.part=ai_failed_failed: The AI draft failed. Try again in a moment.
match.part=ai_failed_timeout: The AI draft took too long. Try again.
match.part=ai_failed_edited: Someone saved the postmortem while the AI was writing, so their text was kept.
match.part=ai_failed_unavailable: AI drafts aren't available right now.
match.part=ai_refused_limit_reached: This workspace asked for as many AI drafts as it can today. Try again tomorrow.
match.part=ai_refused_conflict: A draft is already being written, or the postmortem has text a member wrote.
match.part=ai_refused_ai_unavailable: AI drafts aren't set up on this server.
match.part=read_only: Only responders, admins and owners edit the postmortem.

match.part=incident_hint: The incident, its timeline, updates, follow-ups and postmortem, as one JSON file. Owners and admins only.
match.part=card_description: Download the incidents declared in a date range (UTC) as JSON: timelines, updates, follow-ups and postmortems. Files can be downloaded for 7 days.
match.part=failed_too_large: Too many incidents for one file. Pick a shorter range.
match.part=failed_limit_reached: Too many incidents for one file. Pick a shorter range.
match.part=failed_invalid_args: Pick a range of up to 366 days, the start before the end.
match.part=failed_exports_unavailable: Exports aren't set up on this server.
